lessons.rule: Awake/OnEnable/Start/OnDisable/OnDestroy responsibilities must not overlap without an explicit reason.
lessons.badPattern: Subscribe in Start and OnEnable while only unsubscribing once.
lessons.mastery: Choose one lifecycle owner for registration and keep unsubscribe symmetric.

lessons.rule: One logical gameplay event should have one authoritative registration owner.
lessons.badPattern: Multiple listeners mutate the same gameplay state from different UI/controller paths.
lessons.mastery: Trace event source, registration owner, mutation owner, and presentation listener separately.

lessons.rule: Gameplay state must have one authoritative writer.
lessons.badPattern: UI, controller, and save layer all write HP/gold/inventory directly.
lessons.mastery: Keep mutation in domain/gameplay owner and make UI project results.

lessons.rule: Persistent state, runtime state, defaults, migration, and UI cache are separate responsibilities.
lessons.badPattern: A runtime display fix changes save keys or persistent meaning.
lessons.mastery: Preserve save key semantics unless explicit migration evidence exists.

lessons.rule: Fix ownership or lifecycle ordering before adding a null guard.
lessons.badPattern: Silently return when a required dependency is null.
lessons.mastery: Determine who acquires the dependency, when it must exist, and whether it is serialized, discovered, or injected.

lessons.rule: Damage, hit application, cooldown, status, death, and reward ownership must not be duplicated across UI and gameplay layers.
lessons.badPattern: UI button code applies damage directly while combat system also applies it.
lessons.mastery: Keep authoritative combat mutation in the combat system and let UI invoke commands/project results.

lessons.rule: Coroutines need an owner and stop condition aligned with object/scene lifetime.
lessons.badPattern: Start repeated coroutines on each enable without tracking or cancellation.
lessons.mastery: Tie coroutine lifetime to the responsible component and prevent duplicate concurrent routines.

lessons.rule: Scene and prefab references must preserve their wiring semantics.
lessons.badPattern: Replace serialized references with repeated scene searches to avoid a missing reference error.
lessons.mastery: Repair the reference boundary without creating hidden runtime lookups.

lessons.rule: Per-frame work on Android must be justified.
lessons.badPattern: Find/GetComponent, allocations, LINQ, Instantiate/Destroy, or expensive polling in Update.
lessons.mastery: Cache stable references, use state transitions/events, and pool repeated objects where appropriate.

lessons.rule: Smallest diff is not always safest; smallest correct responsibility repair is the target.
lessons.badPattern: Change one call site while duplicate writers/listeners remain.
lessons.mastery: Inspect equivalent paths before deciding that a one-line patch is sufficient.

lessons.rule: Renaming/removing serialized fields can break scenes, prefabs, and saves even when code compiles.
lessons.badPattern: Refactor field names or types during an unrelated bugfix.
lessons.mastery: Preserve serialized meaning unless migration is explicitly part of the task.

lessons.rule: Destroyed Unity objects can compare as null even when a managed reference exists.
lessons.badPattern: Assume standard CLR null semantics for UnityEngine.Object references.
lessons.mastery: Reason about object lifetime and destroyed-object behavior when diagnosing null/reference bugs.

lessons.rule: Physics mutation belongs in physics-safe timing; presentation/input sampling may belong elsewhere.
lessons.badPattern: Apply physics movement inconsistently between Update and FixedUpdate without understanding ownership.
lessons.mastery: Separate input sampling, physics mutation, and visual interpolation responsibilities.

lessons.rule: Android pause/resume must not duplicate initialization, timers, subscriptions, or save writes.
lessons.badPattern: OnApplicationPause resume path reruns setup that was meant to happen once.
lessons.mastery: Distinguish app lifecycle recovery from scene/component initialization.

lessons.rule: Frequently spawned gameplay objects should avoid unnecessary Instantiate/Destroy churn when pooling is already present or clearly appropriate.
lessons.badPattern: Add a parallel spawn system instead of reusing the existing pool.
lessons.mastery: Reuse existing object lifetime systems and preserve reset semantics.

lessons.rule: UI should represent authoritative state, not become a second gameplay authority.
lessons.badPattern: Button/text code directly rewrites inventory, combat, or progression state.
lessons.mastery: UI invokes existing gameplay APIs and refreshes from authoritative state.

lessons.rule: Do not create a new singleton when an existing responsible system already owns the behavior.
lessons.badPattern: Add Manager2 or another DontDestroyOnLoad singleton as a shortcut.
lessons.mastery: Inspect existing service/component ownership before introducing global state.

lessons.rule: Regression risks must name concrete Unity behaviors.
lessons.badPattern: Use generic warnings such as 'could cause bugs'.
lessons.mastery: Name exact risks such as duplicate subscription after re-enable, stale serialized reference, old save incompatibility, double damage, lost coroutine, or pause/resume desync.

lessons.rule: Only infer structure that is visible in the verified sample or bound repository evidence.
lessons.badPattern: Invent unseen managers, prefabs, or architecture to justify a fix.
lessons.mastery: Mark unknowns and base structural claims on observed code/runtime evidence.

lessons.rule: Teacher analysis is guidance only; verified final code diff is the only answer target.
lessons.badPattern: Train on teacher-generated code that never passed project QA/runtime validation.
lessons.mastery: Bind analysis to QA/CI/runtime-passed final patches only.
